remarks: HEADLINE FINDING: Delhi has a statutory deemed-approval for the Factory Licence that the primary record recorded as 'unclear'. Rule 11A, second proviso, of the Delhi Factories Rules, 1950 provides that if the licensing officer neither grants/renews nor refuses in writing within 60 days from the date of the application, 'licence shall be deemed to have been granted or renewed' (https://labour.delhi.gov.in/labour/chapter-i). The first proviso also deems the premises fully licensed in the interim once a valid application is filed and the fee is paid, so an applicant is legally covered to operate from the date of a complete application.

TIMELINE DISCREPANCY BETWEEN TWO OFFICIAL SOURCES (reviewer should decide which to publish). The operative departmental figure is 30 days: the Labour Department's own 'LIST OF ONLINE SERVICES' page gives a 'Prescribed Timeline (In Days)' of 30 for item 13 'Registration and Grant of Factory License Under the Factories Act, 1948' (https://labour.delhi.gov.in/labour/list-online-services), and the Department's FAQ PDF says the licence 'will be granted within a month'. But the legally notified limit under the Delhi (Right of Citizen to Time Bound Delivery of Services) Act, 2011 is 60 days: Department of Information Technology, GNCTD Notification No. F6(100)/IT/2014/7319-7353 dated 13 August 2014, which amends the Schedule to that Act, lists at entry 233 'Grant of factory license after receipt of complete documents along with prescribed fee | 60 days | Labour' (and at entry 234 'Renewal of license, after receipt of complete documents along with prescribed fee | 60 days | Labour'). Fetched at https://labour.delhi.gov.in/sites/default/files/generic_multiple_files/13_auf_up.pdf — this is a scanned PDF with no text layer, so it was read by rendering its pages to images and reading them (page 1 for the notification header, page 9 for entries 224-238). The 60-day statutory figure is consistent with the 60-day deemed-approval trigger in Rule 11A, which suggests 30 days is an administrative service-level commitment sitting inside a 60-day statutory outer limit.

STALE OFFICIAL PAGE — CAUTION. The Labour Department page 'Procedure of Grant Of Licence' (https://labour.delhi.gov.in/labour/procedure-grant-licence), which is one of the eight verified sources, describes the PRE-DIGITISATION, PRE-2017 process and is contradicted by the Department's own FAQ PDF and by the 2017 gazette. It says documents must be submitted as 'Form No.2 in triplicate' with fee 'paid in State Bank of India, Old Secretariat, Delhi' on a Treasury Challan (T.R.6) in triplicate, and at Question No.15 states: 'The Licence is valid up to 31st December of the year in which it has been granted.' That validity statement is superseded by the Delhi Factories (Amendment) Rules, 2017 (1/5/10 years from the date of grant). The page is nevertheless useful as the only source listing some documents the FAQ PDF omits — a copy of the plan approved under Rule 3A, a copy of the Municipal Trade and Power Licence or proof of connected power load, a copy of the DPCC consent under the Water Act 1974 and Air Act 1981, nomination of occupier documents, and a Health and Safety Policy under Rule 61-G for factories engaged in hazardous process. The DPCC consent requirement is directly relevant to the FGD participant's account of a DPCC-related licence not being received.

STALE FEE SCHEDULE IN THE HOSTED RULES TEXT. The Delhi Factories Rules, 1950 text hosted at https://labour.delhi.gov.in/labour/chapter-i is an un-amended version: its Rule 5 still reads 'for a period of one year or five years' with no mention of ten years, and the Schedule below Rule 5 carries an older and much lower fee table (Nil H.P. row: 20, 50, 100, 250, 400, 750, 1000, 1250; Above 100 H.P. row: 300, 400, 500, 1000, 2000, 3000, 4000, 5000). The current schedule — identical in both the grant FAQ PDF and the renewal FAQ page — is roughly four to five times higher (Nil H.P. row: 100, 200, 400, 1000, 1600, 3000, 4000, 5000; Above 100 H.P. row: 1200, 1600, 2000, 4000, 8000, 12000, 16000, 20000). The FAQ figures were used for the 'fees' check as the current ones. The gazette notification amending the fee amounts themselves was not located and verified this session — only the 2017 notification amending the licence DURATION was. The hosted Rules text should therefore be treated as a reference copy, not as the current operative schedule. Rule 11(2) in that hosted text ('If an application for the grant, renewal or amendment of a licence is rejected, the fee paid shall be refunded to the applicant') is also directly contradicted by FAQ Q12 and Q17, which say the fee is never refunded and is forfeited on rejection — another reason to treat the hosted text as outdated.

ON THE FGD INSPECTION COMPLAINTS. The Department's published inspection procedure (https://labour.delhi.gov.in/sites/default/files/generic_multiple_files/factory.pdf, linked from https://labour.delhi.gov.in/labour/inspection-procedure-timeline-mechanism-flow-chart-checklist) states: 'Presently, no suo-moto inspections are being carried out by the Directorate of Industrial Safety & Health, Govt. of NCT of Delhi. Inspections are carried out by Assistant Directors/ Deputy Directors on the basis of references only. References may be in the form of complaints by trade unions/individuals, complaints in case of FIR received from various police stations, VIP references, renewal, amendment, issuance of fresh licences and directions from Deputy Director/ Director (ISH)...' and 'Inspections are carried out by the officers within 15 working days of receipt of references.' This partially addresses the FGD pain point about 'repeated inspections even after licences have been obtained' — officially there are no suo-moto inspections, but renewal and amendment are themselves listed as inspection triggers, and the document sets no cap on the number of reference-based inspections, so the FGD complaint is not contradicted.

FEE-RELATED RISK NOT IN THE PRIMARY RECORD: FAQ Q12, Q16 and Q17 together mean the auto-calculated fee is forfeited (not refunded) if the applicant fails to supply a sought document within 3 days or if the Service Specification Details are found incorrect and not rectifiable in time, and a fresh application requires paying the fee again. This is a real, quantifiable cost-of-regulation driver that the FGD-only record does not capture.

RENEWAL (RFAL) FIGURES, recorded here only as corroboration since they share the Rule 5 fee schedule: the renewal FAQ page (https://labour.delhi.gov.in/faqs) states renewal must be applied for 'only before 60 days before the due date of expiry of the licence', that a late fee '@25% of the fee payable for a calendar year' applies, and that 'If online application is complete in all respects, Licence shall be renewed within 60 days'. Note that the 60-day renewal turnaround on the renewal FAQ differs from the 30-day 'Prescribed Timeline' the same Department publishes for the renewal service on its list-online-services page.

SOURCES THAT YIELDED NOTHING: https://labour.delhi.gov.in/sites/default/files/generic_multiple_files/number_days_4_oct.pdf (GNCTD IT Dept Notification No. F.6(524)/I.T./2020/4046 dated 4 October 2021, Schedule entries 362-499) and https://labour.delhi.gov.in/sites/default/files/generic_multiple_files/number_days_22_dec.pdf (Notification No. F.6(524)/I.T./2020/Vol.-I/4928 dated 22 December 2021, entries 500 onward) were both read and contain Labour Department entries but NOT grant of factory licence, so neither supersedes the 60-day figure at entry 233 of the 13 August 2014 notification. https://labour.delhi.gov.in/sites/default/files/generic_multiple_files/updated_11.pdf (the 28 December 2011 notification) is a scan with no text layer and was not read page-by-page; it predates the 2014 notification and so would be superseded in any case. https://labour.delhi.gov.in/labour/notifications was fetched and confirms the 2017 gazette is published there as 'Notification for 10 years DFR, 1950' but carries no additional FAL facts.

The transactional portal itself, e-District Delhi (https://edistrict.delhigovt.nic.in/), was NOT fetched this session — the earlier source-list pass recorded repeated TLS connection resets against it. Every portal fact above is sourced from the Labour Department's own published pages describing that portal, not from the portal. All 15 URLs listed in sourcesRead were fetched over https this session and returned HTTP 200.

All verified facts come from a single domain (labour.delhi.gov.in, Office of the Labour Commissioner / Directorate of Industrial Safety & Health, GNCTD), which is the correct authoritative department for FAL in Delhi, but means there is no cross-domain corroboration. The one partial exception is the 13 August 2014 Right-to-Time-Bound-Delivery notification, which was issued by the GNCTD Department of Information Technology and is merely hosted on the Labour Department site.
